newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs to firm, taking aim at 127.34.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs to firm, taking aim at 127.34.

text.p: FUTURE RANGE/DAY SPPRT RSTNC RSI-9 MA-5 MA-25
OUTLOOK OF BOJ OPERATION AT 0020 GMT: Drainage of 600 bln

*JGBs are expected to be firm during Tokyo trade today, buoyed by gains made on Thursday in London that briefly lifted key futures contract to 127.01, with market taking aim at record high of 127.34. *Investor buying of cash bonds likely to lead market higher. *Short-covering of key September in connection with benchmark shift to pick up speed.

Japanese government bonds (JGBs) are expected to be firm in Tokyo trade on Friday after breaking above the key psychological resistance level of 127.00 in overnight London trade, with the market starting to take aim at a record high of 127.34, traders said.

Investor buying of cash bonds, which emerged Thursday, is expected to continue, with operators particularly interested in the longer end and ultra-long 20-year bonds, one trust bank trader said. Life insurers and city banks, which bought bonds on Thursday, are likely to continue this activity today, a securities firm trader added.
Short-covering of the key September futures contract in connection with the approaching benchmark shift is also expected to keep bonds firm.

Although the yen lost ground against the dollar overnight to stand near 117.76 in early Asian time, the possible inhibiting influence of this is likely to be offset by sharp gains in U.S. Treasury bonds on Thursday.
Rises also may slow above 127.00 on wariness about whether bonds are being overbought, but overall bullish sentiment is likely to remain unchanged, the trust bank trader said.
Amid the dearth of other factors, the market will watch Tokyo July department store sales data, due out at 0530 GMT today, although the impact is not expected to be significant.
